<!-- ── Body ──────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<div class="proj-detail-body">
  <div class="proj-detail-prose-wrap">

    <h2 class="proj-detail-h2">About the project</h2>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">Building on a prior initiative that brought immersive space science to nearly 2,000 students, Sarah Treadwell is expanding her mobile planetarium program with a new portable dome system designed for communities that rarely encounter live astronomy education. The project is supported by a 2025 NASA-funded SCoPE Seed Grant through Arizona State University.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">The roadshow runs in two phases: first, sourcing and integrating a dome system compatible with OpenSpace and incorporating visual assets from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory Ocean Worlds Lab; second, deploying the program in underserved schools across the Los Angeles Unified School District, where more than half of students are classified as economically disadvantaged.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">Each event combines an immersive dome show with live scientist presentations and hands-on activities focused on diverse STEM career pathways &mdash; particularly in planetary science, astrobiology, and the search for life beyond Earth. A central theme is NASA's Europa Clipper mission and the possibility of ocean worlds hosting life elsewhere in our solar system.</p>

    <div class="proj-facts-row">
      <span class="proj-fact">NASA Planetary Division</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Portable dome system</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">JPL Ocean Worlds Lab</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">LA Unified School District</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Europa Clipper</span>
    </div>

    <h2 class="proj-detail-h2">How OpenSpace is used</h2>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">The portable dome system is selected specifically for compatibility with OpenSpace, enabling live, data-driven planetarium shows rather than pre-rendered video. Visual assets from JPL's graphics team &mdash; including research vessels and planetary environments from Europa and Enceladus &mdash; are integrated directly into OpenSpace to anchor the program's narrative in real scientific data.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">This approach extends OpenSpace's reach beyond traditional museum and planetarium settings, placing it in school gymnasiums and community spaces where students may never have experienced an immersive astronomy program.</p>

    <div class="proj-quote">
      <p class="proj-quote-text">"By creating immersive experiences that connect ocean research on Earth to the search for life on other worlds, we aim to ignite curiosity, inspire future scientists, and demonstrate that anyone can explore the universe &mdash; no matter where they come from."</p>
      <p class="proj-quote-attribution">Sarah Treadwell, Ocean World's Roadshow PI</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
